subject: Request: trial padding for adapter QA delay (OPS-482)
messages:
From: Lauren Pierce <lauren@opsly.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anil Kumar <anil@opsly.io>
Date: 2026-08-05T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: trial padding for adapter QA delay (OPS-482)

Hi Tessa,

Quick note from our side — we hit an unexpected blocker in QA while validating the Redwood connector for our internal gateway. The adapter is failing intermittently during token exchange (see small extract in adapter-error.log attached). Our engineers are on it, but the root cause looks like an edge case in our certificate rotation that will take a few days to patch and validate end-to-end.

We were hoping Redwood could provide a short runway extension or grant some additional sandbox hours/credits so we don’t lose momentum on the POC. Our timeline is slipping and the team will need another 7–10 days to finish verification and a final smoke test.

Would it be possible to top up our trial by ten calendar days or provide a small token credit (we estimate ~50k tokens) while we resolve this? Happy to share any logs or jump on a call.

Thanks,
Lauren Pierce
Head of Integrations
Opsly Inc

Attachment: adapter-error.log (text, 28KB)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Pierce <lauren@opsly.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: trial padding for adapter QA delay (OPS-482)

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the log. Sorry to hear you’re blocked; we want to keep the POC moving. I looped in Ben (ENG lead on the connector) and David (CS lead) so we can triage fast.

Ben — quick ask: can you take a look at the attached log and confirm whether a short config tweak would get them unstuck? If it’s a code-level fix we can propose a temporary sandbox top-up while we coordinate a fix.

Lauren, two quick requests so we can approve the runway extension internally:
- Confirm whether you need additional calendar days (e.g., +10 days) or token credit (approx # tokens).
- If you can share the exact build id and time window when the failure reproduces, engineering will prioritize.

I’ll follow up with an internal approval note once Ben confirms technical scope.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Pierce <lauren@opsly.io>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: trial padding for adapter QA delay (OPS-482)

Lauren — thanks for the log. I dug in and the failure looks like a certificate handshake retry combined with an unexpected 502 from your gateway when rotation happens. Two options:

1) Short-term workaround: increase the adapter retry window and add a 250ms backoff. This will avoid the transient 502s and should make your QA pass immediately. We can push a connector config patch for your sandbox in ~2 hours.

2) Long-term: deploy a small rotation-stabilizer on your side; our recommended changes are in the attached mutual action plan docx.

Since this is blocking your POC and given the timeline, Redwood can approve the following one-time concession:
- 7 calendar day sandbox extension (immediate)
- 50,000 token promotional credit applied to your sandbox account

We’ll attach the mutual_action_plan_v1.docx outlining next steps and a small checklist. If you accept, we’ll apply the top-up now and schedule a 30-minute troubleshooting call with our engineering lead.

Ben Carter
Lead, Integrations | Redwood Inference
Attachment: mutual_action_plan_v1.docx (docx, 42KB)

From: Lauren Pierce <lauren@opsly.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: trial padding for adapter QA delay (OPS-482)

Thanks Tessa and Ben — much appreciated. We accept the 7-day extension and the 50k token credit. Please apply when convenient.

Per Ben’s suggestion, we’d like the config patch applied to the sandbox first so QA can rerun before the patch hits staging. Our build id is opsly-gw-20260804-rc3 and the failure reproduces most reliably between 09:30–10:00 PST with the certificate rotation trigger.

I’m available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow (2026-08-06) at 11:00 PST or 15:00 PST — what works for you?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Lauren
